findings.title: The retained-proof denominator still contains 198 unproved required rows
findings.impact: The release can be mistaken for ready even though required product behavior remains unproved across C-SDLC v3, corporate Runtime, distributed Runtime, and the current quality gate.
findings.detail: The packet records 143 non_proving rows, 51 source-supported rows without execution proof, and four current gate obligations. Its passing test proves only that the 198-row denominator is counted and routed; it does not supply the missing behavioral proof or a governed amendment.

findings.title: V3-F exact-head proof is stale at the frozen release candidate
findings.impact: The candidate lacks current proof for the C-SDLC v3 parity, rollback, cutover, and operator-approval acceptance surface.
findings.detail: The mapping claims current proof at source 4d641e9, but later candidate changes touched the authenticated C-SDLC surface. The retained validator exits with current_source_drift at candidate fb6cbc7f.

findings.title: The canonical current release-status projection is stale and invalid
findings.impact: Operators receive an outdated release decision and closed remediations appear as open debt; the projection's advertised validator fails on source drift.
findings.detail: The projection is bound to 11a3fe88 rather than fb6cbc7f and still presents now-closed findings including #758 and #759 as current debt. Running current-status/validate.py reports six current_source_drift failures.

findings.title: Issue 519 lifecycle cards contradict its completed publication state
findings.impact: Durable lifecycle truth reports draft, pre-phase, open, unmerged, and not-started states for a final merged publication candidate.
findings.detail: The final candidate packet records a closed issue and merged PR, while SRP remains draft and SOR remains pre_phase, pr_open, not_merged, and not_started. Repair must preserve post-merge card immutability and reconcile terminal truth through the authorized projection/receipt path.

findings.title: Feature-proof coverage contains fourteen corrupted ownership-link suffixes
findings.impact: Canonical release documentation exposes malformed ownership links and the current validator fails to detect the corruption.
findings.detail: Fourteen rows append a stray .com/agent-logic/... suffix after otherwise valid Markdown links at lines 47 through 99. The release documentation validator does not reject this external-link tail corruption.

findings.title: Eighteen GCP-E JSON readbacks are emitted as YAML
findings.impact: Downstream evidence consumers cannot safely parse retained files according to their declared .json format.
findings.detail: The accelerator-type and machine-type gcloud describe commands omit --format=json, so eighteen retained files with .json names contain YAML.

findings.title: Four retained cloud failure artifacts are zero-byte files named JSON
findings.impact: Evidence inventories advertise parseable JSON where no structured failure record exists.
findings.detail: Four failed-command artifacts under issues 730 and 731 are empty. They need explicit structured failure envelopes or a truthful non-JSON naming and manifest disposition.

findings.title: Max-attempt greeting recovery exceeds its retry bound and can poison the durable store
findings.impact: A crash after the final attempt claim can dispatch an unauthorized extra provider operation and then prevent the Runtime from starting because it rejects state that it wrote itself.
findings.detail: Recovery unconditionally increments attempts. A record already at max_attempts becomes max_attempts plus one, dispatches again, and is rejected by valid_for on the next reopen. No test injects a crash immediately after the maximum-attempt claim.

findings.title: Greeting retries replace the stable ledger work identity with attempt-specific IDs
findings.impact: Outbox, result, transcript, audit, and deduplication identities can diverge across retries, fragmenting the durable idempotency contract.
findings.detail: The retry path changes work_id to <stable-key>-attempt-N and refresh propagates that changed value into initiation and ledger metadata. The existing stable-work-key test asserts only the durable record, not the delivered result or ledger-visible identity.

findings.title: GCP mutation approval is self-asserted by the local mutation principal
findings.impact: A process with repository write access and existing gcloud permissions can forge approval and incur cloud mutations or spend without operator consent.
findings.detail: The validator accepts a locally written status=approved plus timestamps without authenticating an operator, signature, MAC, immutable receipt, or out-of-band principal. The negative suite itself manufactures an accepted approved packet.

findings.title: AWS authorization is not cryptographically bound to the saved Terraform plan
findings.impact: Readiness can attest operator approval and resource bounds for different bytes than Terraform eventually applies.
findings.detail: The validator trusts self-declared account verification and authorized_by fields and compares the claimed digest only with a separately mutable text file; it never hashes the saved tfplan bytes or binds the inspected plan JSON to that binary plan.

findings.title: The OBS-B redaction validation lane is vacuous
findings.impact: The named privacy lane can pass while Runtime projections or retained evidence contain actual credentials or provider payloads.
findings.detail: The script only greps a planning bootstrap request for the word redacted. It does not inspect any projected Runtime payload, UI asset, retained evidence, or negative fixture.

findings.title: The real-local Shepherd proof accepts off-host Ollama URLs
findings.impact: A malicious or mistyped environment value can exfiltrate prompts and return forged model digest and GPU-residency evidence.
findings.detail: A starts_with(http://localhost:) check accepts http://localhost:11434@attacker.example, whose parsed hostname is attacker.example. The generated runner then sends the prompt off-host and trusts the remote /api/ps response.

findings.title: Hot-reload cancellation tests can pass without observing a pending reload
findings.impact: The suite can report cancellation behavior as proven even when the watcher never observed the transient write, while fixed sleeps remain scheduler-sensitive in CI.
findings.detail: Both tests sleep for 15ms after a transient write and revert or delete without synchronizing on watcher receipt or pending-debounce state. Generation staying zero therefore passes both the exercised and never-observed cases.

findings.title: Assignment cannot be bound because no candidate SHA was supplied
findings.evidence: Third-party review page 1: candidate identity was absent and the reviewer had no Git access to infer or monitor a revision.
findings.impact: No finding or verdict can be bound to immutable reviewed bytes.
findings.remediation: Supply the finalized immutable candidate SHA and rerun the independent review at that exact revision.

findings.title: Required predecessor #520 was not finalized and had changes required
findings.evidence: Third-party review pages 1-2: the supplied #520 summary retained 14 findings and five P1 findings with remediation #814-#821 still open.
findings.impact: TAIL-05 could not review a finalized predecessor or discharge already-open internal findings.
findings.remediation: Complete the internal remediation wave, finalize #520, and reconcile the exact merged predecessor.

findings.title: Every release-gating row in the milestone projection was blocked
findings.evidence: Third-party review page 2: all 14 feature rows and TAIL-05, TAIL-06, and TAIL-10 were blocked, with 198 remediation rows unproved.
findings.impact: The requested closeout contradicted the milestone's own release projection.
findings.remediation: Recompute the complete release projection only after all remediation proof is current.

findings.title: Code-reduction claim was not verifiable and visible decrease included decomposition
findings.evidence: Third-party review page 2: top-level-only measurements counted moved code as reduction and could not distinguish deletion from relocation.
findings.impact: The recorded metric could prove neither reduction nor its absence.
findings.remediation: Publish a recursive before/after measurement with commands and separate deleted from relocated lines.

findings.title: Triple control-plane coexistence persisted without a current boot-path map
findings.evidence: Third-party review pages 2-3: csdlc-v2, csdlc-v3, and legacy adl surfaces coexisted alongside runtime generations without a per-subsystem execution map.
findings.impact: A fix can land in one generation while the active path continues using another.
findings.remediation: Publish the active per-subsystem boot-path table and retire superseded guidance against parity evidence.
